featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Udupi Shri Krishna Restaurant, which is conveniently located just a 1-minute walk from Matunga East Railway Station—making it extremely easy to reach without any hassle.

I learned that the restaurant was inaugurated by Sane Guruji, which adds a nice historical and cultural touch to the place.

When we arrived, we had to wait in the coupon queue, but it was quite smooth. Within about 10 minutes, our name was called. Considering it was a Saturday, the waiting time was very reasonable. I’ve heard that sometimes the wait can go up to 45 minutes to an hour, but we were lucky.

The staff at the counter was very polite and attentive. One thing that stood out was how they reminded everyone to wash their hands before eating—such a small yet thoughtful and caring gesture.

The food is served on a banana leaf, which adds a traditional and authentic feel. The entire meal felt fresh, simple, and very much like home-cooked food.

The thali included:

2 sabjis
1 koshimbir (cucumber salad)
Roti and puri
Curd
Pickle
Buttermilk
Nimbu rasam and regular rasam
Rice with ghee
One sweet (options like rasgulla, halwa, shrikhand, or gulab jamun)

Curd and sweets are limited, while the rest is unlimited.

The taste was excellent—especially the curd and nimbu rasam, which were absolutely delicious. The rasgulla we had was fresh, mildly sweet, and exceeded expectations.

The management and service were top-notch. The staff ensured that hot food was served in every round, which made the experience even better. Overall, it truly felt like having a comforting meal at home.

The full thali costs ₹300, and the mini thali is ₹200, which is quite reasonable for the quality and quantity offered.

My only suggestion would be to introduce a premium thali option at a slightly higher price, including a few more South Indian dishes for those who want to explore more variety.

Overall, a wonderful experience—highly recommended to everyone! 👍

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mani’s Lunch Home-
Since 2007, during my monthly early morning office tours, I make it a personal ritual to stop at Mani’s Lunch Home in Matunga East for breakfast. No matter how early the day begins or how packed the schedule looks, I always get down here first—it’s my way of starting the day on the right note.
Over the years, I’ve tasted nearly every item served here. But my usual favorites are the idli-vada, medu vada, and the classic sada dosa. The idlis are soft and fluffy, the vadas crispy and golden, and the dosa—light, thin, and perfectly roasted. Each dish is accompanied by hot sambar and fresh coconut chutney that bring out authentic South Indian flavors.
One of the best parts of Mani’s is their warm and generous service. The staff pours unlimited sambar and chutney on your plate until you gently say “enough.” This simple yet heartfelt gesture has become the USP (Unique Selling Point) of the place. It's not just about the food, but the love and hospitality that comes with it.
Once I finish my meal, I always end with a cup of their aromatic filter coffee. Whether you prefer it light or strong, Mani’s coffee is brewed to perfection—rich, bold, and served in traditional steel tumblers that enhance its charm. For health-conscious guests like me, they also offer sugar-free tea, which is light, refreshing, and perfect to start the workday with clarity and balance.
After breakfast, I continue with my day feeling satisfied and refreshed. That peaceful moment at Mani’s sets a positive tone for whatever work lies ahead.
Mani’s Lunch Home is not just a restaurant for me. It’s a monthly ritual, a memory lane of flavors, and a place where time slows down—where every bite takes me back to the roots of comfort and tradition. In a fast-moving city like Mumbai, Mani’s is a calm, soulful corner that never changes.

A school friend sent me a reel about Poe and Pao in Chembur. I decided to go chasing Poe and Pao. Since I was already in Bandra, I thought I’d try their Matunga outlet instead.

Now, if you’re a true-blue Mumbaikar, you know traffic jams aren’t an inconvenience, they’re a lifestyle. So there I was, stuck in the middle of one, wishing for a restroom more than anything else.

When I finally reached, they said, “Go next door.” I stumbled into Dakshin Culture Curry and found the cleanest restroom in Mumbai. Small, but spotless. You can’t do pranayama there, but you’ll definitely come out feeling zen.

Feeling human again, I stepped out… and somehow found myself in Diva Maharashtracha. For a moment, I thought I’d taken a wrong turn in life. That’s when someone explained that Dakshin Culture Curry, Goa Portuguesa, and Diva Maharashtracha are a trilogy, same team, shared menu, different cuisines. And Poe and Pao? The latest addition to the family.

One look at the menu, and I knew there was no way I was walking back to Poe and Pao.

I started with a Sushegad Shot (feni, lime, and kaffir leaves) -  Goa in a glass. Then came the Khekade Kalimiri Soup, a crab-and-black-pepper combo that doubles as a natural sinus reliever. After that, Ravas Moile, Tender Coconut Cashew Nut Sukke (their signature dish), Chicken Modak, and Appam n Amboli.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

Ambience: A+
Food: A+++

What started as a quest for Poe and Pao turned into a delicious detour, a reminder that some of the best finds in Mumbai happen purely by serendipity.

featured_reviews.name: DNB Travel & Food Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
Classic South Indian Favourite with Great Food but Limited Parking

Review:
Cafe Mysore is one of Matunga’s iconic South Indian eateries — an institution famed for its authentic idlis, dosas, rasam vada, and filter coffee that have been delighting locals and food lovers for generations. The food is fresh, hearty, and very reasonably priced, making it a go-to breakfast or lunch spot for both regulars and first-timers. The dosa varieties (especially Dilkhush, Mysore masala) and pineapple sheera are often recommended by customers.

The ambience is casual and simple — not fancy, but clean and welcoming. It’s often busy during peak times (especially weekends and mornings), so be prepared for a bit of a crowd and sharing tables, which contributes to its classic local charm.

What We Loved 👍
Authentic South Indian flavours with generous portions.

Quick service most of the time for breakfast and tiffin items.

Pocket-friendly pricing.

Good for family breakfasts and casual meets.

Seating and comfort are basic; the place fills up quickly during rush hours.

Parking & Access 🚗
There is no dedicated parking lot or valet service at the cafe itself.

Being right on Matunga’s King’s Circle area, finding street parking can be challenging, especially during peak morning and evening hours. You may need to park in nearby public parking areas or use paid parking zones near the circle and walk a short distance.

If driving isn’t convenient, the cafe is very well connected by local transport, with King’s Circle railway station just a short walk away.

Best For: Authentic South Indian breakfast/lunch, quick meals, family outings, casual meet-ups.

It's their warmth that makes the place more than just a restaurant; it feels like a community hub.
Amba Bhavan is more than just a meal; it's an experience. It's a place where you can enjoy fantastic, authentic food in a clean, nostalgic setting, served by people who genuinely care. This is a five-star spot in every sense of the word.

Good taste!!

Location: This place is located at 5 min walking distance from Matunga station East, near Milap store  enroute Khalsa college.

Seating arrangement: The place is tiny roadside food stall without any place for sitting.

Taste: They offer variety of dosas, medu vada, idli, uttapam and taste is amazing. Sambar is burst of flavour and generally served piping hot. My personal fav pick is cheese mysore masala dosa. Chutneys are also fresh and tasty.

Hygiene: One aspect which they should be improving and giving serious attention is cleanliness and hygiene. They wash used utensils to near proximity of eating area. They should try using gloves and caps and sanitation of place is recommended.

Price range: Their price range is ok. Not too costly, not too cheap.

Payment method: They accept payment via cash or upi.

Peak hours: You will generally find the place close to full. At lunch hour the place becomes too crowded but chefs are fast in making dishes and remember the order correctly.

Overall good place to satisfy your south indian cravings but can be improved for customer satisfaction.

A very cozy old Mumbai character place for authentic south indian food. For me the "feast" started with single idli vada dip in piping hot sambar with fresh coconut chutney. Followed by crisp golden roasted Rava masala dosa. I asked for the masla (alu sabji) seperately to maintain the crispness of the dosa till last bite. Again served with sambar, tomato chutney and coconut chutney...the version of dessert here was a first time experience for me here. A slice of bread with neatly trimmed edges, golden roasted in sumptuous butter and sprinkled with brown sugar ... Perfect blend of bit salty and sweet taste with those sugar granules bursting and dissolving in your mouth when they are partially warm. That was an indulging experience...and you think it's over?
Coffee served in small "pyali and katori" to close the perfect deal...
Overall one of the best lunch I had in a company of a very good friend, who introduced me to this place at the first instance.
All served with a smile on face.
If in this part of Mumbai, don't miss the opportunity.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Authentic South Indian Taste in the Heart of Matunga!

Udipi in Matunga truly stands out for serving one of the most authentic South Indian meals in the area. The food tastes homely, fresh, and full of flavour — from the perfectly crisp dosas to the soft idlis and that classic filter coffee which completes the meal beautifully.

What makes it even better is that the entire restaurant is fully air-conditioned, making dining here a pleasant experience even on hot days. The place is clean, well-maintained, and comfortable for families as well as groups of friends.

The service is quick, polite, and efficient — exactly what you’d expect from a traditional Udipi restaurant.

If you’re looking for genuine South Indian food in Matunga that combines great taste, comfort, and a welcoming vibe, this is definitely one of the best spots to visit. Highly recommended!

customer_updates.text: I recently visited Mani's Cafe in Matunga, and my overall experience was excellent! featured_reviews.name: Paras Rewale
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently ordered idli and medu vada from Mani’s Cafe, and I must say the experience was excellent. The idlis were super soft, fresh, and perfectly steamed, just the way authentic South Indian idlis should be. The medu vada was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, not oily at all, and full of flavor.

The real highlight for me was the sambar—it was absolutely awesome! Rich, flavorful, and well-balanced with spices, it tasted homemade and paired perfectly with both the idli and vada. The aroma and taste showed great quality and care in preparation.

Overall, the food felt fresh, hygienic, and made with love. Portion size was good, and everything arrived neatly packed. Mani’s Café is definitely a go-to place for authentic South Indian food, especially if you love a good breakfast.

Highly recommended! 👍

featured_reviews.review_text:
South Indian Food Chain Mani's famous for Quick bite, take away speciallt offering Popular South Indian Dishes like Sada Dosa, Masala Dosa, Cheese Masala Dosa wirh Sumbhar and Chutney, Uttappam Varieties, Snacks, Rasam Vada, Idli Vada, Medu Vada, Milk Shakes, Tea and Coffee. Standing Capacity is around 25 with Few Seats available for Childrens and Senior Citizens.

featured_reviews.name: Bhaskar Basu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ultra fast service. The food is the best tasting South Indian food I have ever had anywhere in India or any South Indian restaurant abroad. It is better than all the other branded South Indian restaurant chains. The spoon just cuts like a knife through the idli. The vada even after being dipped in sambhar does not get fully soggy but somewhat retains its crispiness. The dosas are just too good. The podi variants are numerous and all good. The ukala is tasty too. Feel only the filter coffee gets a 4 out of 5. That is the only one which needs improvement, the filter coffee is good but not the best. No seating arrangement but sufficient area to stand & eat. Well ventilated & covered open standing area to have food. 5 ⭐ restaurant, the best.

Did a repeat visit & felt the need to suggest a few improvements. As it is an open standing area for dine-in customers & also due to the weather there were innumerable flies all around. I know it is tough to control them but more needs to be done rather than insist on just one electronic fly-catcher. Also the employee packing the idlis for online customers was stacking them with his bare hands. And as there were many online and offline customers, the employees were rushed and the employee stacking the idlis used a wiping cloth to dry his bare hands while stacking the idlis. That raises a serious risk of contamination. I know the laws are lax in our country & even if they exist, they are rarely enforced. But we ourselves like responsible citizens should take up cleanliness & hygiene & strictly enforce it without the need for exercise of control by any overseeing authority.

Food quality wise you all are the best, just improve on the hygiene standards. It is always easier for us to dismiss it by pointing to our dirtier neighbours. But when we look inwards & challenge ourselves to be a better version of ourselves, that is the winner's mentality. Set standards that others will want to look up to.

featured_reviews.name: Gerard Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last night, I was there for dinner with my wife, my friend, his wife and son. I wanted to go to Achija. But my friend's son insisted this is a better place. We already had starters at my friend's place. And went for the main course straight. I am an international travel and food writer with a good following worldwide. I understand food, the quality and the devotion or lack of it behind its preparation.

We ordered two paneer dishes with roti, naan etc. All jain.. For the kind of pricing, the food was mediocre. We didn't relish it.  And then we ordered a biryani with the hope that it will uplift our spirits. Same story continues. The biryani made in a hurry had one chief ingredient missing, integrity!

Just ambience and fanfare is not enough. You may survive there with the leftover customers of Achija. But you will succeed only if you can match the quality. Will never visit again. If you can do this to a customer on a weekday with no rush, I can imagine a weekend.

featured_reviews.name: Nishank Anand
featured_reviews.review_text:
Arya Bhavan Run by Muthuswamy this Restaurant has opened in the recent past at Vile Parle east relatively new to western suburbs i have been eating at the OG Matunga outlet bang opp Matunga central Railway Station close to 2 decades now

1.This is the run and owned  by the same family who runs the matunga eatery since day one it opened in vile parle east i started frequenting this place  I must clearly point out my observations for this place
Food is not as perfected like the OG Arya bhavan at matunga i feel that  matunga  has good chefs and service staff to deliver Excellence this vile parle branch offers almost the same menu  but at  times I felt that the food goes haywire chutneys sometimes  are very  well prepared  but some times watery chutneys and half done dosas not done right.

2.i feel  owner should & MUST visit this place atleast 3 times a week though his son and the owner himself know me i feel the service and food here get wonky many  times as they have recently expanded to other branches in sewri chembur too hence staff issue remains a challenge in kitchen as well in service.

3.So the rating 3 is given in comparison with the Original Matunga Arya Bhavan the food otherwise is amazing rite from the masala dosa perfectly made to the Medu vada -is Must try make sure they freshly make it for you when u order it the best perfect medu vada i have ever eaten in mumbai (matunga branch does it right each time everytime) they serve the amazing red green thick freshly made chutneys and perfectly made Sambhar

Thathe idli with podi is perfect

Another hidden gem in the menu is Biscuit Dosa its heaven specially if u like pizzas u will like this Innovatively made dosa styled and made by them.

Idlis are well made nice fluffy perfected with their in-house spl batter u will notice the difference in the first bite itself

They have other variety of dosas like palak dosa Mysore dosa which go well select ur pick

Kanchipuram idli Brahman idli all are good

The best part is they have full ac Restaurant with table service

The service is wobbly which I have complained to the owner once as you have to keep asking people to clean table for water for your food to be served hence I rate service 2star as the staff training is a challenge here getting staff is a bigger challenge in this place hence if they have full strength of staff you might get proper service sometimes they will forget chutneys with dosas hence you will have to ask them for chutneys by the time they get chutney dosa will be over the person who cleans tables may not clean the table properly you may have to ask again for it constantly you will have to ask for water tissue spoon etc ....they may not be proactive it all depends on the staff mood so

While ac works fine washroom is a challenge to use as water soap tissues hygeine are clear issues which owner has to address ASAP

this place  is way above the average south indian Udupi restaurants and its can be termed as a gem for south indian breakfast lovers it does decent "ghati" desi style pizza too few sandwiches freshly made juices and has started chaats

Showstopper is the goti sodas with flavours ,Ananda milk is stocked up and has handmade ice cream which  could definitely be tried chocolate Orange my personal favorite

Coin idli ,butter idli, are all time favorite

Rassam wada is another gem in their menu but have it with pipping hot rasam  and freshly made vada

Their tomato Rasam served here is another favourite's I sometimes come here just to have that however matunga outlet  does it better

Filter coffee is decent served in traditional brass tumbler set with spl sugar

Parking is roadside avoid going on weekends public holidays

Must visit the place after 8.30am before noon on weekdays to avoid  any waiting reservation is not required they are there on swiggy zomato however eating food going there is recommended

Curd rice, bisse bille bhat pav bhaji all is served

Looking for variety seated service with ac  quality food  this is it!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Arya Bhavan by Muthuswamy Caterers in Vile Parle is truly a hidden gem for anyone who loves authentic South Indian cuisine. From the moment you enter, the warm hospitality and traditional ambiance set the tone for a delightful dining experience. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures that guests are well taken care of.

We tried the classic Rava Dosa, Medu Vada, and Filter Coffee, and each item was a burst of flavour. The sambar and chutneys were fresh, aromatic, and perfectly complemented the dishes. The Mini Meals Thali is also a must-try – it offers a great variety of items and feels like a complete homemade meal, full of comfort and taste.

What makes Arya Bhavan stand out is the quality and consistency. The ingredients taste fresh, the hygiene is commendable, and every dish carries the legacy of the Muthuswamy brand. Whether you're visiting for breakfast, lunch, or just a coffee break – this place never disappoints.

It’s no surprise that this place is loved by foodies and families alike. Highly recommended for anyone looking for genuine, soulful South Indian food in Mumbai!

— A very satisfied and happy customer 🌸
